title: Worker queue: fast to answer, slow to finish
question: How long does a queue backlog take to recover after a traffic spike?
description: The API accepts requests, stores them in a worker queue and answers the client at once. Four workers take about 50 ms per job. At 20 s a spike adds 100 req/s for 15 s, more than the workers can process.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the component is up.
Components do not know when their caller gave up; they finish the work and the answer is discarded.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: Clients almost never fail: the queue always answers quickly.
The backlog grows during the spike and drains only well after the spike ends.
The slowest jobs wait tens of seconds in the queue although their clients were answered immediately.
